subject: Discovery recap & proposed trial blueprint — Ledgerly

Subject: Discovery recap & proposed trial blueprint — Ledgerly

Hi Sanjay / Priya —

Thanks again for the time today. Quick recap from our side and a proposed lightweight trial blueprint so we can move to an internal kickoff if this looks right. I kept this short — bolded asks are the things we need to start the setup.

Key pain points (as we heard):
- High false-positive rate on automated reconciliation rules (40–60%) — manual review overhead is the blocker for scaling.
- Latency spikes during month-end processing causing queue backlogs.
- Need for auditability: explainability on why an item was flagged and immutable logs for regulator review.

Primary goals for a 6-week trial:
1) Reduce manual review volume on flagged transactions by 30–50% for top 3 rule categories.
2) Maintain average inference latency < 120ms for batch-size 1 (interactive ops) and < 300ms for bulk scoring.
3) Produce an explainability widget for reviewers showing top-3 reasons for a flag and token-level highlights.

Proposed trial scope (lightweight, low risk):
- Week 0: access + test dataset ingestion (sample CSV of 10k rows), infra access and T&Cs.
- Weeks 1–2: baseline evaluation on historical data (accuracy/precision/recall) and latency profiling.
- Weeks 3–4: integrate prefix/KV caching & simple prompt templates; run parallel scoring.
- Weeks 5–6: compute success metrics, review UX snippets, and decide go/no-go.

Success metrics (what we'll measure):
- Reduction in manual reviews (%)
- Precision@N for the top-3 rules
- Average & p95 inference latency (ms)
- CPU/GPU cost per 1k transactions (for unit economics)

Owners (proposed):
- Redwood engineering lead: Aditya Rao (setup + infra)
- Redwood engagement lead: Dylan Brooks (program manager, weekly sync)
- Ledgerly engineering: Sanjay Mehta (data, access)
- Ledgerly operations: Priya Kapoor (business success, compliance)

Access & Data asks (what we need to start) — please prioritize the first two:
1) Shared S3 link or SFTP + sample dataset (10k anonymized rows).
2) An IP allowlist entry or temporary VPN account for Redwood test agents.
3) A copy of Ledgerly's SOC2 or compliance checklist (we can sign an NDA if needed).
4) A short list of sample reconciliation rules and a representative row schema.

Attachments: pilot-scope-ledgerly.xlsx (draft scope & metrics), access-checklist.pdf (what we need from Ledgerly).

Next steps (proposed):
- Can you confirm data access and an initial point of contact for infra (Sanjay?) by EOD Wednesday (Oct 21)?
- If yes, we’ll schedule a 30-min kickoff (tech + ops) for Mon Oct 25 to walk through credentials and the dataset.

If anything about the goals or metrics is off, call it out and I'll update the scope.

Thanks —
Dylan

Thanks Dylan — helpful summary. Quick confirmations/asks from our side: 

- Confirmed pain focus: reducing manual review headcount for the 'chargeback' and 'duplicate-claim' rules is highest priority. Your 30–50% target sounds reasonable.
- For explainability, the reviewers want both a short natural-language justification and a link back to the original ledger entries.
- We will need a statement on data retention/ephemeral logs — can Redwood commit to 30-day ephemeral logs for pilot agents?

On access: I can provision an S3 read-only bucket with anonymized data by Tue (Oct 20) EOD. For the IP allowlist, I’ll need the Redwood egress IP range.

Compliance: we’re a bit sensitive about any PII — I’ll send a redacted SOC2 summary; if you need a full report we’ll arrange it with our security team (likely requires an NDA).

Happy to run the kickoff on Oct 25 — 10:30am PT works for us.

—San Jay
Sanjay Mehta
VP Engineering, Ledgerly
